turns.text: 2:47 pm update: just got back from Ruiz Family Market with theo in the carrier. delivery is only for diapers now, so saturday market runs are the whole grocery operation. he's asleep on me so typing one-handed sorry. can you help me plan the rest of today and a grocery list + dinners for next week? dinners need to work with oat milk, i'm lactose intolerant. also i'm basically Employee of the Month at Burnt Toast Inc. so keep it simple 🙃

Congrats on the market run with a baby strapped to you, that's a real win. One-handed typing noted, so I'll keep this tight.

**Rest of today (while the baby sleeps on you)**
- Unload the cold stuff first, then sit back down if he's still out.
- Pick 2 dinners to prep partly now so weeknights are easier.
- Do a quick fridge check against the list below.
- When he wakes, take a walk or floor time, then plan for a rough late afternoon.

**Dinners for next week (dairy-free, oat milk friendly)**
| Night | Meal | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Veggie fried rice with eggs | Use leftover rice, no dairy |
| Tue | Sheet-pan chicken thighs + potatoes + broccoli | One pan, minimal cleanup |
| Wed | Pasta with jarred marinara + frozen veggies | Skip the parmesan |
| Thu | Chili (big batch) | Freezes well, eat it for two nights |
| Fri | Chili leftovers over rice | Zero effort |
| Sat | Breakfast-for-dinner: scrambled eggs, toast, fruit | Easy |
| Sun | Tacos with ground turkey, tortillas, salsa, avocado | Skip the cheese or use a dairy-free one |

**Grocery list**
- Eggs, rice, frozen mixed veggies, broccoli
- Chicken thighs, potatoes, ground turkey
- Pasta, marinara, canned beans and tomatoes, chili spices
- Tortillas, salsa, avocado, fruit, bread
- Oat milk (check cooking and coffee uses)

If you tell me what's already in your kitchen and what you can cook comfortably, I can adjust this.

honestly my range is scrambled eggs, boxed pasta and one chili recipe. that's the whole menu. dinners have been takeout or frozen basically every night, last night was takeout with hana again. so the sheet pan thing is ambitious but i'll try it. can you put the plan in table form with prep steps for the two nights i'd actually cook?

Totally fair, then let's build around what you already do well and add just one stretch recipe.

| Night | Meal | Cook? | Prep steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mon | Boxed pasta + marinara + frozen veggies | Yes (easy) | Boil pasta 10 min, microwave the veggies, stir into warm sauce. Skip parmesan. |
| Tue | Takeout or frozen | No | Pick something you like. |
| Wed | Your chili (double batch) | Yes | Brown the meat, add beans, tomatoes, spices, simmer 30 min. Freeze half. |
| Thu | Chili leftovers over rice | No | Reheat and serve. |
| Fri | Scrambled eggs, toast, fruit | Yes (easy) | Use a little oil or dairy-free spread, not butter. |
| Sat | Takeout | No | Treat night. |
| Sun | Sheet-pan chicken thighs + potatoes + broccoli | Stretch | Toss everything in oil, salt and pepper, 425°F for 35-40 min. |

So the cooking is just three easy nights plus one stretch recipe, and the rest can be takeout or frozen with no guilt.

**For the stretch night:** chop the potatoes and broccoli during a nap the day before, store them in the fridge, and the dinner is one tray and a timer.

Want a short checklist for the rest of today, too?
